name: Annemarie Moser-Pröll
milestone_by_age_26: Won the overall FIS World Cup in 1971 at age 17, becoming the youngest ever overall winner, and went on to win five consecutive titles through 1975.
early_history_summary: Moser-Pröll skied from age four in Kleinarl, Austria, skiing downhill daily to reach school. She entered her first FIS World Cup race at 14, won her first World Cup race at 16 in 1969, and became the youngest ever overall World Cup winner at 17 in 1971.
family_context_summary: Born the sixth of eight children to a mountain farming family in Kleinarl, Austria, at 1,230 meters altitude; grew up skiing daily to reach school.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father was a mountain farmer who bent roof shingles for young Annemarie to learn skiing; no formal skiing background in the family.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Austrian ski pipeline, alpine geography, early skiing, coach Charly Kahr, physical talent
evidence_summary: Annemarie Moser-Pröll grew up on a mountain farm in Kleinarl, Austria, skiing from age four and racing from age twelve. She was discovered by local ski teachers Christoph and Stefan Dertnig and joined the Austrian national ski team at fifteen. By seventeen, she won her first World Cup race and the overall FIS World Cup title, becoming the youngest ever overall winner. Her dominance was unprecedented: five consecutive overall World Cup titles (1971-75), Olympic silvers in 1972, and World Championship gold in 1974, all before age 22. The combination of growing up in the Austrian Alps, access to the elite Austrian ski pipeline, and exceptional natural talent made her the most successful female ski racer in history.
starting_point: Born the sixth of eight children to a mountain farming family in Kleinarl, Austria, at 1,230 meters altitude; father was a mountain farmer, mother a farm wife.
current_position: Retired in 1980 after Olympic gold at Lake Placid; ran Café Annemarie in Kleinarl; considered the greatest female alpine skier of all time with 62 World Cup wins and six overall titles.

Won Olympic gold in downhill at Lake Placid and retired from competitive skiing.

name: Alberto Juantorena
milestone_by_age_26: Won Olympic gold medals in both the 400m and 800m at the 1976 Montreal Olympics at age 25, setting world records in both events — the only athlete ever to achieve this double.
early_history_summary: Juantorena was a basketball player at a Cuban state sports school before Polish coach Zygmunt Zabierzowski convinced him to switch to track at 20. Within a year, he reached the 400m semifinals at the 1972 Olympics and was unbeaten in 1973-74.
family_context_summary: Grew up in a two-room house in Santiago de Cuba; parents were unemployed before the Cuban Revolution, later becoming a construction worker and Spanish teacher.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Cuban state sports system, Polish coach Zabierzowski, physical attributes, late specialization
evidence_summary: Alberto Juantorena grew up in a poor two-room house in Santiago de Cuba, initially pursuing basketball at a state sports school from age 14. Polish coach Zygmunt Zabierzowski discovered his running talent and convinced him to switch to track at age 20. Just a year later, he reached the 400m semifinals at the 1972 Munich Olympics, and by 1973-74 he was unbeaten in the 400m. At the 1976 Montreal Olympics, at age 25, he achieved the unprecedented feat of winning gold in both the 400m and 800m, setting world records in both. The Cuban state sports system and his exceptional physical attributes (190cm tall with a 2.75m stride) were the key enabling factors.
starting_point: Born in Santiago de Cuba to a poor family in a two-room house; parents were unemployed before the Cuban Revolution, later becoming a construction worker and teacher.
current_position: Vice Minister of Sports for Cuba; retired from athletics in 1984; considered one of Cuba's greatest athletes and the only person to win Olympic gold in both 400m and 800m.

evidence_summary: Silvia Saint grew up as an only child in communist Czechoslovakia, facing poverty and the early death of her father. She studied management and worked as a hotel manager before entering erotic modeling. In 1996, at age 20, she was named Penthouse Pet of the Year in the Czech edition of the magazine, which launched her career in the adult film industry. She went on to appear in over 300 pornographic films and became the October 1998 Penthouse Pet of the Month in the US edition. Her rise was facilitated by the post-communist opening of the Eastern European adult entertainment market and her physical appearance.

current_position: Retired from the adult film industry since 2001; operates her own website and production company; resides in Prague.

name: Erik De Vlaeminck
milestone_by_age_26: Won the world cyclo-cross championship in 1966 at age 20, the first of seven world titles between 1966 and 1973 — a record for male riders.
early_history_summary: De Vlaeminck grew up in a trailer camp in Eeklo and started cycling as a teenager, initially interested in gymnastics before a hand fracture led him to cycling. He made his cyclo-cross debut in 1962 and won his first world title within four years.
family_context_summary: Grew up in a trailer camp in Eeklo, East Flanders, in a family of travelling clothiers; father raced bicycles.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father raced bicycles, providing early exposure to cycling culture; younger brother Roger also became a champion cyclist and the brothers trained together.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Belgian cycling culture, family cycling background, brother Roger, early specialization, East Flanders
evidence_summary: Erik De Vlaeminck grew up in a trailer camp in Eeklo, East Flanders, in a family of travelling clothiers; his father raced bicycles, providing early exposure to cycling culture. Erik started cycling as a teenager and made his cyclo-cross debut in 1962 at age 17. Within four years, he won his first world cyclo-cross championship in 1966 at age 20, defeating established favorites. He went on to win seven world titles between 1966 and 1973, a record for male riders. His younger brother Roger, who followed him into cycling, became one of Belgium's top road racers, and the brothers trained together, developing specialized techniques in the fields and woods of East Flanders.
starting_point: Born into a family of travelling clothiers in Eeklo, East Flanders; grew up in a trailer camp; father raced bicycles.
current_position: Died on December 4, 2015, at age 70 in Eeklo, Belgium; final role as Belgian national cyclo-cross coach after struggling with Parkinson's and Alzheimer's disease.

milestone_by_age_26: Won Olympic bronze medal in individual sabre at the 2012 London Olympics at age 25, following team gold at the 2006 European Championships and team bronze at the 2006 World Championships.
early_history_summary: Kovalev began fencing at age nine in Russia and rose through the junior ranks, becoming European Junior champion at 15 in 2002 and winning junior World Championship medals in 2005 and 2006. He transitioned to senior competition in 2006, winning team medals at European and World Championships.
family_context_summary: Born in Vesyoly, a small town in the Orenburg region of Russia; started fencing at age nine after pretend fencing as a child.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Russian fencing system, early start at age 9, SKA Saint-Petersburg, coaching, junior champion
evidence_summary: Nikolay Kovalev was born in Vesyoly, a small town in the Orenburg region of Russia, and began fencing at age nine after pretend fencing as a child. He quickly rose through the Russian fencing pipeline, becoming European Junior champion in 2002 at age fifteen and winning silver at the 2005 Junior World Championships. In 2006, at age nineteen, he won team gold at the European Championships and team bronze at the World Championships. His most significant achievement by age 26 was the Olympic bronze medal in individual sabre at the 2012 London Olympics at age 25. The Russian fencing system, with its elite clubs and coaching, was the primary enabling infrastructure.
starting_point: Born in Vesyoly, a small town in the Orenburg region of Russia; family background not documented in reviewed sources.
current_position: Former Russian sabre fencer; now works as a fencing coach in California, United States.

name: Igor Mitoraj
milestone_by_age_26: Held his first solo exhibition at the Krzysztofory Gallery in Kraków in 1967 at age 23, while studying under Tadeusz Kantor at the Kraków Academy of Art.
early_history_summary: Mitoraj attended secondary art school in Bielsko-Biała and entered the Kraków Academy of Art in 1963 to study painting under Tadeusz Kantor. He held his first solo exhibition at the Krzysztofory Gallery in 1967 before moving to Paris in 1968 to continue his studies.
family_context_summary: Born in Oederan, Germany to a Polish forced-laborer mother and a French Foreign Legion officer father who was absent from his life; raised in post-war Poland in his grandparents' village of Grojec.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Tadeusz Kantor mentorship, Kraków Academy, war displacement, emigrant experience
evidence_summary: Igor Mitoraj was born in Oederan, Germany to a Polish forced-laborer mother and a French Foreign Legion officer father who was absent from his life. He was raised in post-war Poland in his grandparents' village and attended art school in Bielsko-Biała before entering the Kraków Academy of Art in 1963. There he studied under Tadeusz Kantor, a renowned painter and theatre director who became a significant mentor and encouraged him to leave communist Poland. In 1967, at age 23, he held his first solo exhibition at the Krzysztofory Gallery in Kraków. He moved to Paris in 1968 and eventually became an internationally renowned monumental sculptor, with his first major solo show at La Hune gallery in 1976.
starting_point: Born in Oederan, Germany to a Polish forced-laborer mother and a French Foreign Legion officer father who was absent; raised in post-war Poland in his grandparents' village of Grojec.
current_position: Died on October 6, 2014, at age 70; internationally renowned monumental sculptor whose works are exhibited in major cities worldwide including London, Paris, Rome, and Tokyo.

name: Per Kirkeby
milestone_by_age_26: Held his first exhibition of drawings and collages in Copenhagen in 1964 at age 25-26, followed by his first solo exhibition at Den Frie Udstillings-bygning and a three-year State Art Foundation scholarship in 1965.
early_history_summary: Kirkeby studied geology at the University of Copenhagen from 1957, participating in Greenland expeditions, before joining the Experimental Art School in 1962. He balanced his geological studies with experimental art, graduating with a master's in arctic geology in 1964 while establishing his art career.
family_context_summary: Born in Copenhagen to an engineer father; grew up on a progressive council housing estate in a suburb of Copenhagen.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Ex-School, Fluxus movement, geology background, state scholarship, Copenhagen art scene
evidence_summary: Per Kirkeby was born in Copenhagen to an engineer father and grew up on a progressive council housing estate in a suburb of the city. He initially studied geology at the University of Copenhagen, participating in research expeditions to Greenland, before joining the Experimental Art School (Ex-School) in 1962 at age 24. The Ex-School, founded by Poul Gernes and Troels Andersen, was a hub of Fluxus-inspired experimentation. In 1964, he graduated with a master's in arctic geology and held his first exhibition of drawings and collages. By 1965, he had his first solo exhibition at Den Frie Udstillings-bygning and received a three-year State Art Foundation scholarship, establishing his dual identity as geologist and artist.
starting_point: Born in Copenhagen, Denmark to an engineer father; grew up on a progressive council housing estate in a suburb of Copenhagen.
current_position: Died on May 9, 2018, at age 79; one of Denmark's most celebrated modern artists, with works in the Tate, MoMA, and Centre Pompidou.
